PPP Lesson • A2+/B1 • Passive Voice

Anna's Beautiful Passive Voice Lesson

Welcome, Anna! Today you will explore passive voice through calm, aesthetic worlds of design, gardening, house building, and psychology. The lesson follows a clear PPP structure: Presentation, Practice, and Production.

Focus: passive voice Grammar: be + past participle Themes: home • garden • mind Speaking + interaction
Lesson goal: by the end of the lesson, Anna will make and use passive voice sentences confidently in beautiful real-life contexts.

P

Presentation

First, review the core grammar. Then play the board game: Anna vs Evgenia.

Rule 1

Present Passive

am / is / are + V3

Use it for facts, routines, and general truths.
The room is decorated in warm colours.

Rule 2

Past Passive

was / were + V3

Use it for finished actions in the past.
The house was built in spring.

Rule 3

Focus on the result

The action matters most

We often do not say who does the action.
Tomatoes are grown here.

Rule 4

Use by only if needed

... + by + person

Add by when the doer is important.
The sketch was drawn by Anna.

Rule 5

Questions and negatives

Is it made? / It is not made.

Put be first for questions and add not for negatives.

Practice

Do the activities. Check your ideas and improve your accuracy.

1. Choose the correct sentence

2. Choose the correct form of be

  1. The flowers planted every week.
  2. The wall built last month.
  3. The room cleaned every day.
  4. The herbs grown in pots.
  5. The books chosen for the reading corner yesterday.

3. Turn the active sentence into the passive

  1. People grow basil in this garden.
    Basil is grown in this garden.
  2. They designed the kitchen in soft green colours.
    The kitchen was designed in soft green colours.
  3. Someone cleans the bathroom every day.
    The bathroom is cleaned every day.
  4. Workers built the house last year.
    The house was built last year.

4. Fix the mistakes

  • The tomatoes are plant in the garden.
  • This notebook was write yesterday.
  • The chair are used for reading.
  • The herbs is watered every morning.

Say the correct versions aloud, then reveal them.

1) The tomatoes are planted in the garden.
2) This notebook was written yesterday.
3) The chair is used for reading.
4) The herbs are watered every morning.
P

Production

Now Anna creates her own language. Use the prompts for free speaking or short writing.

Speaking prompt 1 — Design story

Describe the room. Use at least 4 passive sentences. Example ideas: The sofa is placed near the window. Soft colours are used.

Speaking prompt 2 — Garden tour

Imagine you are giving a tour. Tell what is grown, what is watered, and what was planted last week.

Writing prompt — Peaceful mind

Write 5–6 sentences: How is a peaceful mind created? Use passive voice and your own ideas.

Made for Anna. Passive voice through beautiful design, gardening, building, and psychology themes.
